item.text: I’ll inspect the service documentation first, then build a small read-only reconciliation script that handles pagination, token refresh, rate limits, UTC normalization, deduplication, and per-order half-up rounding. I’ll keep the script outside the deliverable and validate `result.json` before reporting the figures.

item.aggregated_output:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

item.text: The API exposes paged orders plus authenticated customer records, and confirms the page size is 50. I’m going to traverse every reported page, treating repeated order IDs as repeated listings (including non-qualifying orders), while caching each customer lookup.

The full traversal completed successfully after handling the service’s throttling. It found 407 distinct qualifying orders and 20 repeated listings; I’m now writing the required file and checking its schema and arithmetic independently.

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('/workspace/result.json')
d=json.loads(p.read_text())
assert list(d) == ['total_cents','order_count','duplicates_skipped','by_region']
assert set(d['by_region']) == {'north','south','east','west'}
assert all(isinstance(v,int) for v in [d['total_cents'],d['order_count'],d['duplicates_skipped'],*d['by_region'].values()])
assert sum(d['by_region'].values()) == d['total_cents']
print('valid', d)
PY"
